name: Fire Drill: Proving Ground
why: All three agents pivoted Fire Drill, and this version has the deepest core: deterministic provenance enforcement on money-moving tools plus a measured breach-versus-utility table, keeping the live judge phone call.

name: Netting House
why: Still the most real system as written: an LP, invariants and a two-phase commit move the money, and Claude handles the mess a script cannot.

name: Memory Blame
why: An original engine (lineage graph, bisect, cascade rollback) for a documented, unsolved memory-poisoning problem, with a crisp demo.

name: Vault Heist
why: Ground-truth settlement in reducers plus a service-rate constraint makes it a measurable security-versus-utility system; keep the constraint, not the bounty marketplace.

name: Refactor Insurance
why: The soundest version of the proof-by-failing-test idea all three agents converged on: limited to no-behavior-change PRs, a differential test is a mechanical proof.

name: Render-Parity Shield
why: B independently reached the same render-parity core as my A-P2; it is a real, measurable system that works on any page without staged cheaters.

name: Netting House
why: Still the biggest, most frequent real-money pain in the pool, with a mechanism proven to free 1-5% of GDP in liquidity a year.

name: Fire Drill + Callback
why: Two agents independently reached the same pivot: a callback on every payment turns Fire Drill into a control that blocks today's BEC losses.

name: Tripwire
why: Containment with very few false alarms for the agent attack that cannot be prevented, needed by every company that connects agents to private data.

name: Intent Diff
why: A daily, growing pain for every team merging agent PRs, with a clear per-PR metric.

name: Parity Proxy
why: Two agents converged on the defensive Two-Face; A's visibility engine makes it measurable and protects agents on every page today.

name: Fire Drill + Callback
why: Fire Drill with a real callback, which B independently converged on (B-P8); use A-P1's provenance policy as the trigger so the fix holds however the attacker words it, and the demo ends with a second phone ringing.

name: Netting House
why: Rigorous build with a basis-points network business and the deepest Fetch.ai use; name Cycles and Causa Prima before the judges do.

name: Two-Face KYM: Know Your Merchant for agent cards
why: Keeps Two-Face's cloak-switch demo and its Bright Data and Elastic fit, but sells to the agent-card issuers who actually lose money; the defensive shield variants (A-P2, B-P2) are features without a payer.
